August, 2024

Author: Pankaj Bhatia
Bench: Pankaj Bhatia
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:55758

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 8697 of 2024

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Applicant :- Mohit Kumar
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. Lko.

And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Pradeep Kumar,Anshuman Singh,Karan Srivastava

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
None has appeared for respondent no.2 despite notice.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.278 of 2024, under Section 363, 376 IPC &
Section 4(2) of POCSO Act, P.S. Mankapur, District Gonda.

3. In terms of the FIR it was alleged that on 07.06.2024, daughter of the informant was missing Mohit Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175944074/
1 since 1 PM and was enticed by some unknown person.

entities.text: Mohit Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Subsequently, in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she was friendly to one Eklavya and were in talking terms with him for the last 3 to 4 months, however, they had broken up.
She stated that thereafter she met the applicant and was in talking terms with him for the last two months.

She further stated that the applicant had asked her to come as he had promised to marry her and thus, she left on the said date and went alongwith her earlier friend Eklavya on a bike to railway station Mankapur where after leaving her, her friend came back and thereafter, when she reached Lucknow, the applicant refused to meet her and thereafter, the victim came back to Gonda.
In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she stated that the applicant had come to meet her at Lucknow and thereafter, physical relations were formed and thereafter, she left.
She also stated that the victim administered beer before physical relations were formed.
The victim has refused to undergo medical examination.
4. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

5. Considering the statement of the victim that she had gone out of her own freewill to Lucknow where she met the applicant and considering the huge inconsistencies in the two statements coupled with the fact that the victim refused to undergo medical examination, the applicant who is in custody since 14.06.2024 and has no criminal history, is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Mohit Kumar be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 13.8.2024 nishant  Mohit Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175944074/
